DiagnosticReport.conclusion:
1. No pulmonary embolism.
2. Dilated ascending aorta measuring 4.4 cm. Recommend annual follow-up imaging with CT angiography or MR angiography.
3. 5 mm hepatic hypodensity, too small to characterize. In a patient without known malignancy, no follow-up imaging is needed.
4. Mild dependent atelectasis.

_sections.title: CLINICAL INDICATION
_sections.text: Acute shortness of breath and right-sided pleuritic chest pain 2 days after a 4-hour flight. Elevated D-dimer.

_sections.title: TECHNIQUE
_sections.text: CT angiography of the chest was performed after intravenous administration of 75 mL iohexol 350 using a pulmonary embolism protocol. Multiplanar and MIP reformats were reviewed. CTDIvol: 9.8 mGy. DLP: 352 mGy-cm.

items.label: Pulmonary arteries
items.text: Adequate opacification of the pulmonary arteries. No filling defect to the subsegmental level. Main pulmonary artery measures 2.7 cm.

items.label: Thoracic aorta
items.text: The ascending aorta measures 4.4 cm at the level of the right pulmonary artery. No dissection or intramural hematoma. The aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta are normal in caliber.

items.label: Heart
items.text: Heart size is normal. No pericardial effusion.

items.label: Lungs and airways
items.text: Mild dependent atelectasis in both lower lobes. No consolidation. No suspicious pulmonary nodules. Central airways are patent.

items.label: Upper abdomen
items.text: 5 mm hypodensity in hepatic segment 6, too small to characterize. Otherwise unremarkable.
